analysis.title: Will Rubner Stay Undefeated? Citadel Securities Chief Strategist Says "Path Of Least Resistance" Is Higher As Semis Hit 13.8x
key_insights: Citadel Securities strategist Scott Rubner (note 'November: The Setup Improves', Nov 4, 2026) says the election clears the deck to rebuild equity exposure into year-end, citing light positioning, returning corporate demand, persistent retail buying and post-midterm seasonality.
Over the past month the Nasdaq 100 fell almost 10% and semis fell more than 20%, while the equal-weight S&P rose 4-5%. Rubner reads this as money changing addresses, with little broad-based selling.

Retail has been a net buyer of US cash equities on Citadel's platform for 22 consecutive sessions since October 5, about $33B, the sixth-longest and fifth-largest streak since 2017. Daily buying averaged $1.5B, 1.4x the trailing-year average. Of 12 prior streaks of at least 15 sessions, the S&P rose in 10, with a median gain of 2.2%.

Year-to-date retail net equity buying is a record $251B, above the previous full-year high of $241B in 2021 and 134% ahead of the same point last year. Semis took 38% of single-stock retail options premium, roughly double their share a year ago.
Morgan Stanley's QDS desk estimated retail sold $1.4B of US equities on Monday, the second net-selling day of the year. Citadel's platform data through Nov 3 shows the buying streak intact.

Buyback eligibility: less than a quarter of S&P 500 index weight in mid-October, about two-thirds by Election Day, with Rubner expecting 85% by November 9. New buyback announcements total $1.5T through Nov 2, above the 2025 full-year record. October added $166B, more than twice the historical average.

Rubner's CTA model puts aggregate US equity positioning at -3.3 standard deviations, below the 2nd percentile of its one-year range and the lowest since March 31. CTAs have been short 26 straight sessions. A sustained recovery through key technical levels could trigger mechanical buying.

Q3 earnings: 83% of the first 304 reporters (65% of index weight) beat, versus a ~75% historical average. The index-weighted average earnings-day move is -1.2%, the second worst in 87 seasons. In Tech and Communication Services, over 90% beat but only 35% and 18% traded higher.
Since June 30, forward EPS estimates rose 32% for Memory, 31% for AI Infrastructure and 30% for Semis, while forward P/Es fell 50%, 36% and 35%. All 20 S&P 500 semiconductor names de-rated.
Nasdaq 100 trades at 19.1x forward earnings, the lowest since October 2022 and 24% below the January peak, with a 5% premium to the S&P, the smallest since January 2017. It was 21.7x a month ago.

S&P 500 semiconductors trade at 13.8x forward earnings (17.1x a month ago), 45% below the January peak and a 25% discount to the S&P, the widest since December 2018. The group is expected to deliver nearly half of Q3 index EPS growth with under a fifth of the weight.

On Wednesday the Nasdaq beat the SOX by nearly 460bps. Goldman's desk saw rotation into hyperscalers with semis used as a source of funds. Zero Hedge argues a Democratic Congress could slow data center builds, so 13.8x may reflect a smaller build-out.

Equal-weight S&P gained over 4% while the Nasdaq 100 fell almost 10% over 20 sessions through Nov 2, a 14% divergence in the 99th percentile since 1990. On Oct 29, 406 of 503 constituents rose while SPY fell 38bps, the broadest positive breadth on a down day in Citadel's history.
Concentration: top 10 names are 37% of index weight, Mag 7 are 33%. Rubner argues renewed buying in big tech would have an outsized effect on the benchmark.

Volatility: VIX rose above 21 with S&P one-month realized vol below 11. One-month implied vol is above the 95th percentile of its one-year range in Energy, Comm Services, Staples and Health Care, and in the 83rd and 96th percentiles for the S&P and Nasdaq 100. SPY put skew is in the 73rd percentile. Rubner expects a vol crush to let vol-targeting strategies rebuy equities.

Seasonality: since 1950 the S&P has been higher six and twelve months after every midterm, with a median 12-month gain of 14.5%. Q4 of midterm years averaged +5.6% vs +2.9% for all years. The Q4 low was set in October in 14 of 24 midterm years, followed by a median rally of nearly 10%.

Zero Hedge agrees the index likely grinds higher but doubts semis lead, citing data center CDS at fresh 2026 highs and hyperscaler executives saying building will be harder. Brent is still in the $90s.

sector_views.rationale: Rubner sees a sentiment rebound in semis as the biggest upside lever at 13.8x forward P/E. Zero Hedge doubts it, citing rotation into hyperscalers and data center build-out risk.
Rubner says a modest sentiment recovery in Technology could have a meaningful impact on the broader index given compressed valuations.

earnings_insights: Q3 S&P 500 earnings: consensus entering the season was 27% YoY EPS growth. Through the first 304 reporters (65% of index weight), 83% beat EPS estimates, versus a ~75% historical average (basis not stated in the source).

Index-weighted average earnings-day move is -1.2%, the second worst in 87 reporting seasons since 2005. More than 90% of Tech and Communication Services companies beat EPS, but only 35% and 18% traded higher.
Forward EPS estimates since June 30: +32% Memory, +31% AI Infrastructure, +30% Semis. Forward P/Es fell 50%, 36% and 35% over the same period.
Semis are expected to deliver nearly half of the S&P's Q3 EPS growth with less than a fifth of index weight.

trade_ideas.description: Rebuild US equity exposure into year-end, with a Nasdaq 100 and semis sentiment rebound as the main upside lever (Rubner, Citadel Securities)
trade_ideas.rationale: Light positioning, returning buybacks, retail buying, vol crush and post-midterm seasonality create a mechanical bid into year-end.
trade_ideas.risk: Semis may keep de-rating if data center build-out slows under a Democratic Congress.

risk_factors: Semis were used as a funding source for hyperscalers on Wednesday, and a Democratic Congress could make new data center builds harder.
Data center CDS is at fresh 2026 highs.
Brent in the $90s and the Iran war remain unresolved.
Retail flow data conflicts across desks (Morgan Stanley QDS vs Citadel).
Concentration: the top 10 names are 37% of S&P weight, so weakness in big tech would weigh on the index.
Earnings beats are not being rewarded, with an average earnings-day move of -1.2%.
vol_and_positioning: VIX rose above 21 while S&P one-month realized vol was below 11.
One-month implied vol is above the 95th percentile of its one-year range in Energy, Comm Services, Staples and Health Care. S&P is in the 83rd percentile and Nasdaq 100 in the 96th.
SPY put skew is in the 73rd percentile.

CTA model positioning is -3.3 standard deviations, below the 2nd percentile of its one-year range and the lowest since March 31. CTAs have been short 26 straight sessions, and were at +1.7σ three months ago and -1.0σ one month ago.
Retail net buying on Citadel's platform runs 22 straight sessions, about $33B, with $251B year-to-date, a record.
SPW vs NDX hit its lowest since April 2000 on October 7. The ratio is now in the 82nd percentile of its one-year range and its 14-day RSI is the most overbought in more than two years.
Buyback-eligible S&P 500 index weight was under a quarter in mid-October, about two-thirds by Election Day, and Rubner expects 85% by November 9.
geopolitical: Democratic sweep in the midterm elections, which JPMorgan had flagged as the likeliest outcome.
JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the GOP's losses, and oil fell 8% on Wednesday.
Brent remains in the $90s amid the Iran war.
Meta's Dina Powell McCormick said data center builds are 'going to be harder' under the new political regime.
cross_bank_references: Morgan Stanley's QDS desk estimated retail sold $1.4 billion of US equities on Monday.
JPM's desk is saying the same thing on post-midterm seasonality.
JPMorgan had flagged on Monday a Democratic sweep as the likeliest outcome and the worst one for stocks.
Goldman's desk saw 'the clear rotation into hyperscalers with Semis being used as a source of funds.'
Goldman's Garrett sees seven signs of 'healing' but said 'We just have to survive 2026 first.'

tension_points.bull_case: Rubner says semis at 13.8x forward P/E, a 25% discount to the S&P, with forward EPS up 30% since June, mean a modest sentiment recovery could lift the broader index.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman's desk saw semis used as a funding source for hyperscalers, data center CDS is at 2026 highs, and a Democratic Congress could slow builds, so cheap can get cheaper.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Semis continuing to underperform the Nasdaq and hyperscalers after the election, as on Wednesday when the Nasdaq beat the SOX by nearly 460bps.

tension_points.bull_case: Rubner cites CTAs at -3.3σ, 85% of index weight buyback-eligible by November 9, retail buying streak, vol crush and midterm seasonality as a mechanical bid into year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: Beats are being sold, with an average earnings-day move of -1.2%, Brent is in the $90s, and the Iran war remains unresolved.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 'first half of November positive nearly 80% of the time' seasonal pattern failing in mid-November.
